plainLanguage: Two main nerves supply the chest muscle, an upper one and a lower one, but dissection studies find the pattern varies from person to person and that other nerves contribute too.
qualifiers: A clean one-nerve-per-head account is a simplification: a Sihler-stained series reports the muscle mainly innervated by the lateral pectoral nerve with an intercostal contribution in every specimen.
Two independent series report three constant pectoral branches rather than two.
The 62 and 38 per cent figures for the medial nerve's course are reported in the source as attributed to earlier work, not measured there.

The intercostal contribution was established by Sihler whole-mount nerve staining on five randomly selected muscles, not on all 80 specimens. Eighty is the gross-dissection total. Any statement about intercostal contribution rests on those five.
Donor mean age in this series was 69.3 (SD 11.8) years, range 48 to 90.

statement: The pectoralis major is innervated by the pectoral nerves, with the lateral pectoral nerve supplying the proximal part of the muscle and the medial pectoral nerve the lower part; primary dissection series report substantial variation in this pattern, including three trunk-level pectoral nerves and an intercostal contribution.
